definitions.explanation: Something that has gone missing or been lost. A somewhat old-fashioned or literary word, still used in everyday speech in some regions and in certain set phrases.

examples.japanese: {失|う}せ{物|もの}が{見|み}つかった。
{失|う}せ{物|もの}が{出|で}てこない。
examples.english: The missing item hasn't turned up.

examples.japanese: {失|う}せ{物|もの}のお{守|まも}りを{買|か}ったら、なくした{鍵|かぎ}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: After I bought a charm for finding lost things, I found the keys I had lost.

notes:
Has a slightly old-fashioned or traditional flavor. Particularly associated with prayers and charms at shrines for recovering lost items ({失|う}せ{物|もの}{探|さが}し). The verb {失|う}せる means to vanish or disappear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {失|う}せ{物|もの}が{見|み}つかる: a lost item is found
- {失|う}せ{物|もの}{探|さが}し: searching for a lost item
- {失|う}せ{物|もの}のお{守|まも}り: charm for finding lost things
- {失|う}せ{物|もの}{封|ふう}じ: ritual to find lost items

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {落|お}とし{物|もの}: dropped item, lost property — the standard modern term used at police stations and lost-and-found counters
- {忘|わす}れ{物|もの}: forgotten item — something left behind accidentally, especially on trains or at shops
- {紛失物|ふんしつぶつ}: lost property — formal/official term used in legal or administrative contexts
